sources.title: Pierre Deligne, Theorie de Hodge II, Publ. Math. IHES 40 (1971) 5-57. Complete PDF fetched and inspected (14 MB extraction to text, printed pages 5-57).
sources.locator: SS4.1, printed pp. 40-42 (Theoreme 4.1.1(i)-(ii): Leray degeneration for proper smooth f and surjectivity of H^m(Xbar,Q) -> H^0(S,R^mf_*Q); its proof uses the topological codimension-two surjectivity pi_1(S^s)->pi_1(S) on p. 41 and the Gysin left-inverse argument); SS4.2.1-4.2.4, printed pp. 43-44 (continuous families of Q-Hodge structures, polarizations, the conditions (4.2.2.1)-(4.2.2.4), the algebraic category of a dense Zariski open); SS4.2.5, printed pp. 44-45 (closure of the algebraic category under tensor, sum, direct factor, Tate twist, integral lattices, and (4.2.2.4) via (4.1.2); propagation of algebraicity from a dense open; R^mf_*Q is algebraic); SS4.2.6-4.2.8, printed pp. 45-47 (semisimplicity of the pi_1-representation, the minimal-dimension-sum argument with the determinant-line/torus step (4.2.7), and the commutant/centre corollaries).

contents.name: Theoreme 4.1.1(i): degeneration of the Leray spectral sequence in rational cohomology for f proper and smooth over a smooth separated base
Theoreme 4.1.1(ii): surjectivity of H^m(Xbar) -> H^0(S,R^mf_*Q) for a smooth compactification, giving the invariant image
The topological step in the proof of 4.1.1: pi_1(S^s,s) -> pi_1(S,s) is surjective because the complement has topological codimension at least two
4.2.1-4.2.4: continuous families of Q-Hodge structures, polarizations, the closure conditions, and the definition of algebraic families via a dense Zariski open and a projective smooth f
4.2.5(i): the algebraic continuous families are closed under direct factor, direct sum, tensor product and Tate twists, and satisfy the polarizability and integral-lattice conditions
4.2.5(ii)-(iii): algebraicity on a dense Zariski open propagates to the family, and R^mf_*Q of a proper smooth f is algebraic
4.2.6: the pi_1-representation on the fiber of any family satisfying (4.2.2) is semisimple
4.2.6 footnote: extension of the semisimplicity statement to all variations by unpublished Schmid results
contents.reason: The footnote relies on unpublished 1970 Schmid results for arbitrary analytic variations; this pair proves the geometric-polynomial-algebraic case by its own fixed-part and socle route and states no analytic-variation claim.

contents.name: 4.2.7: for a rank-one local subsystem whose tensor power is trivial, tV stays locally constant; the determinant-line argument for the minimal-dimension subsystem
4.2.7's abbreviation that the sum W of the minimal-dimension complex subsystems is defined over Q
4.2.8: the commutant algebra is semisimple with a Hodge structure of type (0,0) centre, and the twisted subsystems tW are isomorphic
contents.reason: These corollaries about the commutant algebra and isomorphisms of twisted subsystems are not consumed by any claim or proof of this pair; the semisimplicity theorem uses only 4.2.6-4.2.7.

sources.title: Claire Voisin, Hodge structures and the topology of algebraic varieties, author-hosted lecture notes (Harvard CMSA revision), 70 pp.
sources.locator: SS3.1, printed pp. 36-38 (Theorem 3.1 Leray degeneration for smooth projective families and Theorem 3.2 the decomposition Rf_*Q = sum R^qf_*Q[-q] in the bounded derived category); SS3.2, printed pp. 38-41 (the identification H^0(Y^0,R^kf_*Q) = monodromy invariants, Theorem 3.3 the global invariant cycle theorem H^k(X^0_Y,Q)^inv = Im(H^k(X,Q) -> H^k(X^0_Y,Q)), Corollary 3.4 that the invariant part is a Hodge substructure with base-point-independent isomorphism class, Corollary 3.5 that Hodge components of invariant classes are invariant, and the proof via Theorem 2.7 strictness and W_kH^k(X^0) = Im(H^k(X) -> H^k(X^0))).

contents.name: Theorem 3.1: the Leray spectral sequence of a smooth projective family degenerates
Theorem 3.2: Rf_*Q decomposes as the direct sum of its shifted cohomology sheaves in the bounded derived category
Theorem 3.3: the global invariant cycle theorem, equality of the invariant subspace with the image of the restriction from a compactification
Corollary 3.4: the invariant part is a Hodge substructure whose isomorphism class does not depend on the reference point
Corollary 3.5: every Hodge component of a monodromy-invariant class is itself invariant
The proof route of Theorem 3.3: strictness of mixed Hodge morphisms plus W_kH^k(X^0) = Im(H^k(X) -> H^k(X^0))
Corollary 3.7: classes with finite monodromy orbit form a Hodge substructure
contents.reason: The finite-orbit Hodge-substructure corollary is not claimed by this pair; only the invariant (trivial-orbit) fixed part and full semisimplicity are built here.

contents.name: Theorem 3.8 and Proposition 3.9: Hodge classes have finite monodromy orbit, and the variational Hodge conjecture under the Lefschetz standard conjecture
contents.reason: The Hodge-locus finiteness machinery and the variational Hodge conjecture are not claimed, consumed or prerequisite for the fixed-part and semisimplicity results of this pair.

sources.locator: Chapter 3 Transversality, printed pp. 25-33 (transversality of maps, Propositions 3.2-3.5; stability of transversality and Corollary 3.12; the measure-zero calculus Lemma 3.15; Baby Sard Corollary 3.18; equidimensional Sard Theorem 3.20; the density/perturbation form of the transversality results).

contents.name: Corollary 3.12: transversality to a closed submanifold is stable on a compact source under small perturbations
Lemma 3.15 and Corollary 3.18 (Baby Sard): measure-zero sets are closed under countable unions and subsets, and a C^1 map from a lower- to a higher-dimensional Euclidean space has measure-zero image
Theorem 3.20 (equidimensional Sard) and the general Sard results of SS3
contents.reason: The general Sard theorem and the manifold-level measure-zero calculus are authored and published on the sard-theorem-and-transversality page of this run; this pair only consumes the parametric-transversality and generic-avoidance consequences through the declared published items.

contents.name: The transversality of maps and submanifolds of Propositions 3.2-3.5 and the fibre-product theorem
contents.reason: The general transversality theory is published on the sard-theorem-and-transversality page; this pair consumes only the submersion perturbation family and parametric transversality as declared dependencies.
